sections.content:
You know *por un lado* as an ordering marker from B1 Unit 23. This lesson uses it as the first half of a pair, to weigh two sides of one question:

• *Por un lado, …; por otro (lado), …*: "on the one hand … on the other". Give one side first and the other second. Use it when something has an advantage and a drawback, or when there are two points of view.
• *Por una parte, …; por otra (parte), …*: the same pair, a little more formal.
• You can make the second half sharper with *en cambio*: *Por un lado, el piso es barato; en cambio, está lejos del centro.*

Put a comma after each half-opener and a semicolon or a full stop between the halves. The second half needs *otro* or *otra*, never a second *un lado*.

sections.title: Weighing two sides
rows: Por un lado, vivir en el centro es cómodo; por otro, es ruidoso.
On the one hand, living in the centre is convenient; on the other, it is noisy.
Por una parte, me gusta el trabajo; por otra, gano poco.
On the one hand I like the job; on the other I earn little.
Por un lado, el piso es barato; en cambio, está lejos del centro.
On the one hand the flat is cheap; on the other, it is far from the centre.
Por otro lado, el barrio es muy tranquilo.
Also, the neighbourhood is very quiet.

sections.content: *Por otro lado* can also appear alone, to add a new point ("besides", "also"), as in the last example. The full pair is for weighing two things against each other.
